clue.text: Such creatures take food smothered in fruit

indicators.note: something smothered in a covering is wrapped up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: grapes are a fruit
to take food is to eat

explanation.surface: Some animals eat their dinner buried in fruit, the way a gorilla might feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such creatures' points back at the picture of animals eating fruit, which suits gorillas and chimps.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimpanzees and orangutans are the creatures meant; the clue's fruit-eating picture describes them.

clue.text: Make a deep cut in good tree

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon is told to slice deeply into a healthy tree.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this means to slash or wound something deeply.

clue.text: Love affair so begins, finally finding god

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A romance starts and ends up with the god of love himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' works on each of Love, affair, so and begins in turn, taking each word's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the Greek deity of love, Cupid's counterpart, so he is a god.

clue.text: Labour embraces works producing fertile ground

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: labour means hard work, toil
OPS is short for opera, Latin for works

explanation.surface: The Labour Party takes in some factories and ends up with farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party but is just hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper layer of earth is the rich soil in which plants grow, the fertile ground.

clue.text: Expert turned up in case of poison nut

indicators.note: in places the reversed expert inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
in a down clue turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist discovers a poisoned nut in a murder case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes ECA, set inside P and N, the outside letters of poison.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known edible nut from a hickory tree of North America.

clue.text: Poets supporting strike-breaker keeping weapons here

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other one

parts.note: a scab is someone who works during a strike
bards are poets

explanation.surface: Poets back a worker who crosses the picket line, with weapons stored nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' in a down clue puts BARDS beneath SCAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaths for swords and daggers are where those blades are kept when not in use.

clue.text: A university will accept decline for so long

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: to decline, of a plant or creature, is to die away

explanation.surface: A university is resigned to falling standards for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a stretch of time, but it is the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye; this one is borrowed from French.

clue.text: Turned out exhausted after a time

indicators.note: the exhausted piece comes after a time, so it follows them

parts.note: exhausted means tired

explanation.surface: Someone was worn out after a stretch of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' looks like 'happened' but means dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be well turned out is to be dressed smartly, so the phrase means clothed.

clue.text: Sets off researches forgetting victory in Europe

indicators.note: forgetting something means leaving it out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to research a matter is to investigate it
VE Day marked victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: A historian studies the war but skips the triumph in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a process is to start or provoke it, the same as initiating it.

clue.text: This actor may be unconscious and read

parts.note: a patient who is under is anaesthetised, unconscious
to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: A player might be knocked out and still be reading a script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read' in the sense of reading a subject at university, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in performer learns a lead role to take over if needed, the kind of actor meant here.

clue.text: Exclusive small pen

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a coop is a pen for poultry

explanation.surface: An upmarket little writing implement is being advertised as a luxury item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is not for writing but an enclosure for hens.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a story one paper gets before all its rivals is called an exclusive.

clue.text: Charles Edward must accept one's punished

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the shortened names hold the other piece

parts.note: Ted is a pet name for Edward
one's read as a contraction is one is, giving I and S

explanation.surface: Bonnie Prince Charlie must accept what he has coming to him.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Edward Stuart, Bonnie Prince Charlie, was the Young Pretender; the surface invokes him, but the two names work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Being scolded or disciplined severely is to be castigated, a synonym of punished.

clue.text: Effective obstacle that's quickly broken?

parts.note: a sound plan is one that works, effective
a barrier is an obstacle

explanation.surface: A useful obstruction that turns out to be easily smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quickly broken' suggests flimsiness, but means broken by something going fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft travelling faster than about 760 mph pass this point, so it is broken by speed.

clue.text: Agrees to allow use of chavs in action

indicators.note: in action means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Authorities consent to employ rowdy youths in some kind of operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Chavs is British slang for brash young people in flashy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant something graciously, condescending to permit it, is to agree to allow it.

clue.text: Delight oppressing a Conservative spilling secrets?

indicators.note: to oppress is to weigh down on, so in a down clue this piece sits on top

parts.note: to revel in something is to delight in it
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A gleeful bully crushes a Tory politician, who then leaks everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that reveals or discloses hidden truths is eye-opening, as though spilling secrets.

clue.text: Finished drink, finding common ground

parts.note: over means done, finished
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: Two people finish their drinks and find they agree on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two areas share a region, that shared area is ground they hold in common.

clue.text: Advancement in marketing?

definitions.meaning: advancement means a rise in rank, as when an employee goes up a grade
marketing means publicising a product, as in a sales campaign

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both moving up a job ladder and publicity drives for goods.

clue.text: Worker on set mostly looking happy

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the worker comes after the other piece
mostly means not all of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a radio is a set, as in a wireless set
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A crew member on a film set seems cheerful most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a film set but is a radio set; 'mostly' cuts its last letter to give RADI.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaming person glows with joy, so a happy face is described as glowing.

clue.text: Friends regularly showing sign of embarrassment

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pals keep showing up blushing.
explanation.definitionFit: A blushing face turns this colour, so the colour is a sign of embarrassment.

clue.text: I'm off toast!

definitions.meaning: I'm off is what someone says when leaving, a goodbye
a toast is a call made when raising glasses, like 'cheers'

explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' looks like bread, but it is the salute made with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal British word is a farewell and also a drinking salutation.

clue.text: Soldiers left part of church seeing deterioration

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: Troops leave a bit of the church and notice it is crumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling back into illness or bad ways after improving is a worsening of the condition.

clue.text: Pay out to cover American delay

indicators.note: to cover something is to go over and around it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to pay out money is to spend it
US stands for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: Someone must hand over money to make up for a hold-up in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone or hold something off for a while is to put it on hold, delay it.

clue.text: Star's cooler patch on a tropical beach?

definitions.meaning: the Sun has darker, cooler regions on its surface
a tropical beach is a spot in the sun, a whimsical second reading

explanation.definitionFit: The term names cooler dark areas on the Sun, and playfully a sunny holiday location.

clue.text: Cash obtained by son — a full term at work

indicators.note: at work means busy or operating, so these letters are set to work and rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy earns money by working a whole school term.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes in 'son' too: SON plus A FULL TERM give the twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sum of money is jokingly called this, so it stands for cash.

clue.text: Symbol of bear market's origin

parts.note: to bear is to carry, to tote

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it begins, its first letter

explanation.surface: An emblem marks the start of a falling stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear market' is the trading term for falling prices, but 'bear' here means carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved pole or emblem representing a clan is a sacred symbol.

clue.text: Democrat supporting battle for part of constituency

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece is below the other

parts.note: a war is a battle

explanation.surface: A Democrat backs a fight in one district of an electoral area.
explanation.definitionFit: An electoral area is split into smaller administrative divisions for local councillors.

clue.text: Bits of garden furniture?

parts.note: they are pieces of furniture for sleeping on, and parts of a garden where flowers grow

explanation.definitionFit: Flower plots in a garden share their name with the furniture for sleeping on.

clue.text: Pay for picture, creating an impression

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for something
a print is a picture

explanation.surface: Buying a painting makes someone look good to guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating an impression' suggests making a good showing, but the impression is a mark left by a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark pressed into the ground by a foot is a physical impression.

clue.text: Identify delicate material found by back of shop

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: A detective recognises fine fabric discovered behind a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To place someone is to recognise or identify where you know them from.

clue.text: Tailor having a bit of modesty left

indicators.note: a bit of means only a section of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A dressmaker leaves the client a touch of modesty.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to design or fashion it to suit, which is to shape its look.

clue.text: Made notes about worms

indicators.note: about means moved round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A biologist jotted down observations on earthworms.
explanation.definitionFit: These are roundworms, a large group of slender worms.
